absent: Pending-table synchronization mechanics and redistributor register effects beyond the pass-through skip.
Complete ITS register region table contents and per-register read or write semantics.
Device, collection and translation-entry allocation, lifetime and locking beyond shown call sites.
ABI revision history, entry size values and guest table address decoding details.

findings.text: Enables logical interrupt handling for a virtual CPU by conditionally synchronizing its pending table; synchronization is skipped when the redistributor pass-through marker is set and otherwise performed.
Reports whether guest table writes are in progress from distributor state, permitting memory writes without a running virtual CPU during that window.
Exposes the ITS as a managed device type with creation, destruction, attribute presence, attribute read and attribute write handlers bound under one operations descriptor.

Creation validates the requested device category, allocates zeroed ITS state, initializes command and table mutexes plus device and collection lists and a translation cache, marks the base undefined, records message-interrupt and ITS presence flags, seeds default table base attributes, attaches private state and selects the newest table ABI; when already initialized it also runs early setup under the configuration mutex.
Region lookup resolves a guest offset to its descriptor by binary search over a caller-supplied sorted region array.

User register queries and accesses enforce offset-dependent alignment: low and high identifier ranges accept word granularity while the central control range requires double-word granularity; unaligned offsets or unknown regions are rejected.

Base address registration is single-shot: the first address is recorded and published on the MMIO bus with ITS handling, while a later attempt fails as busy; register access requires a defined base and otherwise reports absence.

Address attribute writes validate the selector, copy the base from the caller, range-check it against overlap rules, register the IO device and initialize debug state; reads return the stored base; register attributes move one value between caller and region handlers with length from the matched region width and writes preferring a userspace handler when present.

Save sorts devices and per-device translation entries by ascending identifier, chains entries with capped forward deltas, writes packed little-endian values carrying validity plus sizing or routing fields, emits zero for entries lacking a collection, skips device identifiers outside the current base window without failing, and appends one invalid terminator when the collection area is not fully filled.

Restore rejects malformed data including zero or too-small interrupt identifiers, forward jumps beyond device event capacity, oversized event-bit counts, unknown or duplicate collections, absent routing targets, and identifiers outside the active base window; allocation failures propagate and trigger release of the partially built device or collection lists.
Base registration holds the slot mutex across the undefined check, address assignment, descriptor setup and bus publication.

Register attribute access nests the global VM mutex, then an opportunistic all-VCPU acquisition that aborts busy on contention, then the configuration mutex; VCPU and VM locks are released on all paths.

Control operations for reset and table save or restore nest global VM mutex, opportunistic all-VCPU acquisition, configuration mutex and ITS table mutex in that order; initialization bypasses locking as a no-op.

Creation holds the configuration mutex while probing initialization state and publishing defaults; destruction holds the ITS table mutex while tearing down debug state, freeing device and collection lists, invalidating caches and destroying the translation cache. A build-time declaration acquires command then table mutex to document nesting.

Guest table scanning uses a callback contract where the walker reads one fixed-size guest entry at a time from successive addresses and the callback returns the stride to the next candidate; zero or negative results terminate with that status and overrunning the declared span terminates successfully. Scratch storage is pre-cleared to the entry size.

ITS instance state organizes devices and collections as linked lists plus a translation cache, with separate command and table mutexes, a base address starting undefined, an enable flag defaulting off, and stored bases for device, collection, command and property tables.

Device and translation-entry comparators order elements strictly by ascending device identifier and event identifier respectively, giving deterministic save order and enabling forward-delta computation.

Version-zero persistence saves device tables before collection tables and restores in reverse order; restore supports flat and indirect level-one device tables by paging through fixed-size chunks, treats an all-invalid scan as success, and discards partially restored software state on failure.

Commit encodes the active ABI entry widths into the stored collection and device bases without altering other fields; reset clears valid markers, enable state and command queue pointers and releases all software device and collection objects while retaining ABI sizing fields.
Saving a translation entry backed by hardware state without newer virtualization support fails the whole save; per-device saves otherwise stop at the first guest write error.

Default table attributes request inner write-back caching with outer matching inner, inner shareability, and for the main bases a large page size; device and collection bases add their respective type codes and the property base uses only the cache and share defaults.

The device advertises address, control and register attribute groups: one address selector for the ITS base, control selectors for init, reset, save and restore, and a register group delegated to region validation; init succeeds immediately while other control selectors dispatch under locks to reset or to the active ABI table handlers.
